title: Weight-Space Programming for Medical Imaging: Do We Still Need Training Data?
domain: medical imaging (chest X-ray, breast ultrasound, abdominal CT, pelvic MRI)

headline_result.text: Networks written in one tool-free reply reached mean test AUC 0.719 (Opus) and 0.711 (Astra) on six MedMNIST tasks, beating zero-shot MedSigLIP (0.588) but below the same network trained with Adam on 256 labels (0.828).

key_claims.claim: Both LLMs wrote all weights in a single reply with no tools, no feedback and no image.
key_claims.quote: You have no tools: no code execution, no calculator, nothing to run, and you will not see any image from this

key_claims.claim: The same network trained with Adam on 256 labels beats the written networks on every MedMNIST task.
key_claims.quote: with Adam on 256 labels is better on every MedMNIST task

key_claims.claim: On SynthUterus, a task the LLMs are unlikely to have seen, Opus reached AUC 0.764 while Astra's three networks were far below chance (0.136).

notes_for_review: A clean, restrictive test of write-from-scratch WSP: single tool-free reply, small CNN, seven medical tasks, three calls per model, with both a label-free foundation-model baseline and gradient training on the same architecture. The result is mixed: above chance and better than a handicapped zero-shot MedSigLIP on 5 of 6 tasks, but a few hundred labels win everywhere, and the one low-contamination task shows an LLM confidently writing an inverted classifier. Evidence that the LLMs know MedMNIST class priors weakens the 'from medical knowledge alone' framing; no random-weight control is reported.
